query: I'm the only data person for a regional business unit. We get about 350 free trials a month and roughly 45 of them convert. Sales wants a propensity-to-convert model so reps only call the trials most likely to close. I've got 14 months of trial data with about 40 features from the CRM. Plan the model for me.
expected_behavior: Says this is not fundable as a model at this volume, and says why: fourteen months hold about 600 conversions in total, an out-of-time window of three months holds about 130, and the top decile of that window contains a dozen or so; the lift at that operating point cannot be separated from the base rate, and a model that cannot be validated cannot be believed, whatever the training metrics say. Does not plan the model anyway. Hands back what works at this size: a rule on one or two fields (for example trial activation depth or company size), written down with the metric it will be judged on, and the volume at which a model would become checkable (a few hundred conversions in the validation window alone, so several times the current rate). Adds that the rule's effect on close rate is itself measured by a holdout against how reps pick today, not assumed. Without the skill, the model typically plans the propensity model with cross-validation and feature engineering, at most warning that the data is small.
